mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in a month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 1% in a month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the CPIAUCSL is above 2% YoY, the real interest rate becomes negative, which typically leads to increased investment in equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals a supportive monetary policy for a growing economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: economic expansion with accommodative monetary policy
failure_condition: If INDPRO > 12-month MA and FEDFUNDS < 2% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances.
